title: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself)
points: Every piece of knowledge or logic should have a single authoritative place.
Duplication means a bug fix must be made in many places.
trade: Don't merge code that merely looks similar but changes for different reasons (coincidental duplication). A wrong abstraction costs more than duplication.
test: Two methods look identical today but belong to different business rules. Should you DRY them? Why or why not?
answer: No. They change for different reasons, so merging couples two rules. Keep the duplication until the shared knowledge is real.

questions.question: Two validators are identical today but enforce rules owned by different teams. What should you do?
options: Merge them into one shared class now
Leave them separate until the shared knowledge is real
Move both into a static utility
questions.explanation: This is coincidental duplication. They change for different reasons, so merging couples unrelated rules.
